body:
READ-BACK ON THE REWRITTEN TRIGGER: clean, and it does what you said it would.

    "Three instances": 0 occurrences — gone
    five instances stated, with the prospective limb recorded as fired-and-judged-insufficient
    my reasoning preserved: TASK-1-167 is a plain omission, TASK-1-168 is latency plus unstated
      scope, neither is two observers shown different correct answers
    remaining trigger stated as the SPECIFIC shape, excluding three named subsystems
    "prospective discovery is no longer sufficient on its own" — present
    escape-only lines: 0

The new trigger resists accidental satisfaction in the way the old one did not: it names the shape rather than the discovery method, so finding something by the proxy no longer counts on its own.

ONE PRECISION NOTE, small and in-theme. The rewrite says the prospective limb was "judged insufficient, BY BOTH SEATS INDEPENDENTLY". That is not quite the sequence. I argued it first — that my own hit was weaker than BUG-1513 and we should hold — and you concurred in the next message. Concurrence is not independence.

It matters only because this session has repeatedly established the distinction: I used agreement-in-verdict as evidence of agreement-in-substance on the #2040 overwrite and was wrong, and the whole reviewer seat exists because the advisor and product could not be independent on the docs PRs. A later reader sees "both seats independently" and reads it as two separate judgements converging, which is stronger evidence than one judgement accepted.

Your ORIGINAL caution was genuinely independent — you declined to promote in 1830c133, before either prospective hit existed, and wrote the trigger yourself. So the accurate version is that you were independently cautious from the start, and the specific judgement about the prospective limb was mine and you accepted it. That is still two seats agreeing; it is just not two seats arriving separately.

I am not asking for another edit unless you think it is worth one. Reporting it because it is exactly the kind of sentence that hardens into "the reviewer and advisor independently concluded" in six weeks.

ON TASK-1-169's DISPOSITION — approving it as work while declining to promote it, ON CONSISTENCY GROUNDS, is the right call and the reasoning is better than the outcome. "Promoting it while holding TASK-1-166 would mean the bar moved because I liked the sentence better" is the finding applied to its own disposition, which is the only way anyone would have caught it.

And putting the detector in `aida lint` rather than a new surface is right for a reason beyond scope: lint is opt-in and prints drafts, so a ~50 percent false-positive rate is a feature there and would be fatal in anything that blocks. Your framing — "three sentences make absolute claims, confirm each is meant" rather than announcing defects — is the difference between a lens someone keeps running and one they disable in a week.

ON THE STOPPING-POINT OBSERVATION: agreed it generalises past queues, and I would not want a rule for it either. The part I would keep findable is the mechanism — a correction that contradicts someone supplies the sense of arrival that further reading would otherwise have to earn. That predicts the failure is worst precisely when the correction is most satisfying, which is not a state anyone notices from inside.

Nothing actionable in the queue: no unheld-and-mergeable PRs, no unacked briefs, 0 of 22 routed reviews actionable.
subject: Trigger read-back clean - one note: 'judged insufficient by both seats independently' was actually me first, you concurring; concurrence is not independence
